scope.assessment: No proven filename/path traversal, shell-argument injection, or header injection defect found. Publication and rename use content-provider APIs; source titles do not become private filesystem paths or command options.

evidence.observation: Rename rejects separators, controls, format characters, dot/dot-dot and excess length. Publication filenames replace path separators, control and format characters and require an alphanumeric extension.

Content-Disposition input is bounded, decoded defensively, reduced to a basename, stripped of controls, and given a validated or MIME-mapped extension. OutputStore applies Safety.filename before publication.
Metadata and download output templates use fixed local basenames. Format IDs use a narrow allowlist and literal filter selectors; mapped extensions use an allowlist.
Arguments are passed as a ProcessBuilder list, without a shell.
Recovered choices validate extension and format ID. Task directory paths validate UUIDs.
Replayed If-Range tags reject CR/LF and other ASCII control bytes.

evidence: Safety.kt:106 truncates in UTF-16 code units.
PublicationReceipt.kt:24 appends the task identifier to the final display name.
LibraryRepository.kt:173-176 reads the actual name returned by providers after rename.
test_gaps.gap: Very long multibyte titles and supplementary Unicode at truncation boundaries need provider acceptance coverage. Static review does not prove failure because providers may normalize or truncate names; no defect is asserted.
No source edits, builds, devices, emulators, network calls, or test execution were performed. Existing source tests were inspected only.
